description.p: Skykeep brings your iCloud notes, reminders, calendar, contacts, Drive and photos to your computer as fast desktop apps. Your library is kept on this machine, so everything opens straight away, even offline, and what you change here reaches your iPhone and your other devices.

Sign in once with your Apple Account. Your password stays on this computer, in your system keyring. Skykeep connects to Apple for your iCloud, and to the calendars you subscribe to and the calendar accounts you add yourself; the AppImage also checks GitHub for new versions of Skykeep. There is no Skykeep account and no analytics.

Skykeep is an independent, open-source project. It is not made by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Apple, and it reaches iCloud through interfaces Apple has not published, so Apple may change them at any time.

screenshot.caption: Skykeep, with your six apps and your account

description.p: Notes keeps what you typed when you quit, close its window or sign out. Two Apple Accounts on one computer never mix: reminder and event alerts, the Hidden album's lock, calendar subscriptions and unfinished downloads stay with their own account, and signing in as someone else starts clean. Favorite, Hide and Delete in Photos are kept safely until iCloud has them, even if Skykeep closes first. Lists open faster with large libraries, each app's window loads only its own app, and typing with an input method no longer acts on half-typed words. Skykeep has its own colours and sign-in, an Open-Source Licences window in Settings, and an updated SQLite with a security fix.

Saving over a file in the iCloud Drive folder keeps it the same file in iCloud, so apps on your other devices that follow it, such as a password manager's database or a document left open, still have it, and its earlier versions stay in iCloud. Notes can put a link on the words you select, with Ctrl+K or from the Aa menu, and offers a link you have just copied. Open at Login waits for the tray before keeping the window closed. When iCloud is busy, an app's tile says so in a few words, and Calendar asks again on its own when a connection stalls.

Every app's window has a sidebar button, at its top left or with F9, that hides the sidebar and brings it back, remembered for each app. Calendar can add Nextcloud and other CalDAV calendars beside iCloud's, with Nextcloud signing you in on its own page. A small Calendar window brings your calendars over the month from its More menu, a small Drive window its places from the sidebar button, an event's popover stays on screen as it grows, Keyboard Shortcuts shows the app in front and is never cut off, and Send to iPhone has its own icon. A reminder set for a time with no time zone shows and rings at that time wherever you are.

Skykeep now opens to a launcher of your six apps, each showing what it holds and how fresh it is; Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Drive and Photos each open in their own window, and Settings fit on one calm page. Downloading large iCloud Drive folders no longer crashes Skykeep, notes save cleanly every time, and every sidebar moves with the arrow keys.

Send files to your iPhone from your file manager's right-click menu, back up every photo and everything in iCloud Drive to a folder or drive you choose, and see iCloud files' thumbnails in File Explorer. Each app now has its own icon. Photos upload several at once, files go into notes again, and Reminders syncs even when an alarm holds a date no calendar has.

Skykeep stays signed in and never sends a code to your iPhone on its own, works with Advanced Data Protection, downloads whole iCloud Drive folders, keeps both edits when an event changes on two devices, and stays fast with very large photo libraries.

Skykeep starts on every Windows PC with nothing else to install, says why when it can't pick up your session or Apple asks you to wait, saves your sign-in reliably while Windows Defender checks the file, and leaves updates to Scoop when Scoop installed it.
When Apple doesn't accept a password, Skykeep now says so plainly, and that an app-specific password can't sign in.

Every Apple ID signs in, an AppImage for Ubuntu 22.04 and newer, a locked Hidden album in Photos, Keep Both or Replace when pasting in iCloud Drive, drag and drop inside windows on Windows, and fixes across every app.
The first release of Skykeep: iCloud Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, iCloud Drive and Photos as six desktop apps with one sign-in, kept on your computer and in sync with your iPhone.

ul.li: Notes and Reminders changes from your iPhone usually arrive in about a second
Everything opens instantly and works offline, and your edits sync when you reconnect
A note edited here and on your phone at the same time is merged, not overwritten
Search across every app, quick capture, and reminder alerts with Complete and Snooze
Export Everything to Markdown, iCalendar, vCard and your original files
